entry.title: [UPDATED] GO-2026-5039: Arbitrary inputs are included in errors without any escaping in net/textproto
entry.content:
Arbitrary inputs are included in errors without any escaping in net/textproto

Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-42507, CVE-2026-42507

Affected:

  • stdlib — fixed in 1.25.11, 1.26.4

When returning errors, functions in the net/textproto package would include its input as part of the error. This might allow an attacker to inject misleading content to errors that are printed or logged.

References:

  • https://go.dev/issue/79346
  • https://go.dev/cl/777060
  • https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/tKs3rmcBcKw

entry.title: [UPDATED] GO-2026-4947: Unexpected work during chain building in crypto/x509
entry.content:
Unexpected work during chain building in crypto/x509

Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-32280, CVE-2026-32280

Affected:

  • stdlib — fixed in 1.25.9, 1.26.2

During chain building, the amount of work that is done is not correctly limited when a large number of intermediate certificates are passed in VerifyOptions.Intermediates, which can lead to a denial of service. This affects both direct users of crypto/x509 and users of crypto/tls.

References:

  • https://go.dev/cl/758320
  • https://go.dev/issue/78282

entry.title: [UPDATED] GO-2026-4946: Inefficient policy validation in crypto/x509
entry.content:
Inefficient policy validation in crypto/x509

Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-32281, CVE-2026-32281

Affected:

  • stdlib — fixed in 1.25.9, 1.26.2

Validating certificate chains which use policies is unexpectedly inefficient when certificates in the chain contain a very large number of policy mappings, possibly causing denial of service. This only affects validation of otherwise trusted certificate chains, issued by a root CA in the VerifyOptions.Roots CertPool, or in the system certificate pool.

References:

  • https://go.dev/cl/758061
  • https://go.dev/issue/78281
  • https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/0uYbvbPZRWU

entry.title: [UPDATED] GO-2026-6218: Avoid quadratic complexity in resolvePath in net/url
entry.content:
Avoid quadratic complexity in resolvePath in net/url

Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-56860, CVE-2026-56860

Affected:

  • stdlib — fixed in 1.25.13, 1.26.6, 1.27.0-rc.3

Previously, resolving relative paths containing parent directory ('..') segments performed string conversions and buffer rewrites on each step, resulting in quadratic time complexity and high memory allocation overhead. Now, path resolution operates on a byte buffer using index-based backtracking for '..' segments, eliminating the quadratic time complexity and significantly reducing memory allocations.

References:

  • https://go.dev/cl/803681
  • https://go.dev/issue/80494
  • https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/94pEornpRlI

entry.title: [UPDATED] GO-2026-4341: Memory exhaustion in query parameter parsing in net/url
entry.content:
Memory exhaustion in query parameter parsing in net/url

Aliases: BIT-golang-2025-61726, CVE-2025-61726

Affected:

  • stdlib — fixed in 1.24.12, 1.25.6

The net/url package does not set a limit on the number of query parameters in a query. While the maximum size of query parameters in URLs is generally limited by the maximum request header size, the net/http.Request.ParseForm method can parse large URL-encoded forms. Parsing a large form containing many unique query parameters can cause excessive memory consumption.

References:

  • https://go.dev/cl/736712
  • https://go.dev/issue/77101
  • https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/Vd2tYVM8eUc

entry.title: [UPDATED] GO-2026-6090: Limit handshake messages we are willing to accept post-handshake in crypto/tls
entry.content:
Limit handshake messages we are willing to accept post-handshake in crypto/tls

Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-56862, CVE-2026-56862

Affected:

  • stdlib — fixed in 1.25.13, 1.26.6, 1.27.0-rc.3

Handshake messages, such as KeyUpdate, are always considered as state-advancing, regardless of whether a handshake has been completed or not. As a result, a malicious client can keep sending KeyUpdate messages to force the server to keep performing key derivation operations indefinitely.

References:

  • https://go.dev/issue/80528
  • https://go.dev/cl/804261
  • https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/94pEornpRlI

entry.title: [UPDATED] GO-2026-4870: Unauthenticated TLS 1.3 KeyUpdate record can cause persistent connection retention and DoS in crypto/tls
entry.content:
Unauthenticated TLS 1.3 KeyUpdate record can cause persistent connection retention and DoS in crypto/tls

Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-32283, CVE-2026-32283

Affected:

  • stdlib — fixed in 1.25.9, 1.26.2

If one side of the TLS connection sends multiple key update messages post-handshake in a single record, the connection can deadlock, causing uncontrolled consumption of resources. This can lead to a denial of service. This only affects TLS 1.3.

References:

  • https://go.dev/cl/763767
